questions.questionText: Which one of the following best describes mandated choice?

options.text: A limited range of options is provided
Individuals are required by law to choose an option
Options are framed to influence the outcome of decisions
The option is selected automatically if an alternative is not chosen

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows a production possibility diagram for an economy where goods and services are produced in the private and public sectors. The economy is currently producing at point Y. Following a change in government, it is decided that the output of public sector goods and services should be increased by VW. What is the opportunity cost, in terms of private sector output, of this reallocation of resources?

options.text: OS
OT
ST
YZ

questions.questionText: Which one of the following best describes how a social scientist would develop an economic theory?

options.text: Apply logic to make connections between normative and positive economic concepts
Create a hypothesis and test whether it can predict the behaviour of economic agents
Develop a number of policies and test whether they are successful in the real world
Form a set of value judgements and test whether they are supported by statistical data

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to lead to an increase in the number of people who are frictionally unemployed in the UK?

options.text: A fall in the number of Jobcentres provided by the government
A persistent fall in reported levels of consumer confidence
A reduction in the rate at which Jobseeker’s Allowance is paid
A significant real terms increase in the National Living Wage

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to indicate that a government is trying to cause a significant change in the pattern of economic activity?

options.text: A reduction in the rate of tax on income from retirement pensions
A reduction in the tax on a good with positive consumption externalities
An increase in the rate of an inheritance tax
An increase in the tax on a good with very inelastic demand

options.text: Diseconomies of scale
Falling labour productivity
Increasing marginal returns
Increasing returns to scale

questions.questionText: A large company experiences a significant fall in its year-end profits. Reports suggest it is a consequence of the divorce of ownership from control within the company. Which one of the following is most likely to explain why the divorce of ownership from control may have harmed the firm’s performance?

options.text: As part of their earnings, managers receive profit-related pay and share options
Due to the satisficing principle, managers act in the interests of shareholders
Moral hazard means shareholders take more risks to achieve greater rewards
Profit maximisation is not the most important objective for all managers

questions.questionText: Table 4 shows the index of consumer prices and the unemployment rate for an economy. The data is for the end of each quarter in a particular year. The index of consumer prices for the final quarter of the previous year was 120.9. According to the data, it can be concluded that

options.text: prices were lower at the start of the year and employment was lower at the end of the year.
the quarterly inflation rate fluctuated whilst the unemployment rate increased throughout the year.
the relationship between the change in the inflation and unemployment rates was positive in each quarter.
there was an inverse relationship between prices and unemployment in each quarter.

options.text: Commercial banks’ deposits with the central bank
Notes and coins held by households
Savings deposited with commercial banks that have more than a year to maturity

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to lead to individuals who are currently in relative poverty remaining in relative poverty?

options.text: A major housebuilding programme helps to reduce the number of workers who are geographically immobile
Average earnings in an economy rise more slowly than the increase in the national minimum wage
The government changes the income tax system in a country to make it more progressive
The rate of increase in the price of necessities, such as energy, is higher than for all goods and services

In Country Y, the production of rowing boats requires two and a half times as many resources as the production of canoes
The maximum number of canoes and rowing boats that Country X and Country Y can produce between them is 400
The opportunity cost of producing a canoe in Country Y is 25% lower than it is in Country X

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a supply-side policy that is most likely to lead to an improvement in the balance of trade in goods and services on the current account of the UK’s balance of payments?

options.text: A significant and sustained reduction in Bank Rate by the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of England
Deregulation that makes it easier for UK transnational corporations to invest abroad
Increasing the supply of pounds on the foreign exchange market to reduce the exchange rate and make exports cheaper
Tax breaks for manufacturing firms that invest in upgrading their machinery and other capital goods

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements regarding UK competition policy is correct?

options.text: An objective of competition policy is to reduce firms’ profits by preventing firms from charging prices that are higher than their marginal cost of production.
Competition policy aims to increase social welfare by discouraging existing firms from entering new markets that have a low concentration ratio and are already very competitive.
Competition policy recognises that a monopoly may be preferable to many small firms producing in a competitive market due to the existence of diseconomies of scale.
High concentration ratios and consumer complaints are examples of indicators which may suggest anti-competitive behaviour and prompt further investigation by the Competition and Markets Authority.

questions.questionText: A government announces that, over a 10 year period, it plans to reduce the number of tradable pollution permits it issues each year. Which one of the following is the most likely response from firms in industries affected by the announcement?

options.text: Firms are likely to delay investment into more environmentally friendly production methods
Only the firms that generate the most pollution are likely to react at all
Over time, more firms will have an incentive to reduce their pollution
The firms with the lowest costs of reducing pollution will buy the most permits

questions.questionText: All other things being equal, which one of the following is most likely to be a consequence of inflation in the UK?

options.text: The amounts outstanding on households’ existing mortgages will fall in real terms
The nominal value of people’s incomes before tax will fall
The price of all goods and services sold in the UK will increase
The real value of the money deposited in commercial banks will increase
